reviews.title: Fast, good price, and runs well
reviews.comment: Works great and fast! Great value when I purchased it, upgraded a pc from 2 sticks of 8 to 4 sticks of 8gb. Despite the other sticks being another brand they work together well and no crashes!
reviews.author: Austin

reviews.title: Good RAM
reviews.comment: Got these back in summer of 2025 before the RAM armageddon. Was $60 for a set of 4. These work great for mid tier computers, look really nice, and function as intended. I havent had any issues with them since ive had them.
reviews.author: Jane

reviews.title: Great ram for the price
reviews.comment: I’ve been running this RAM since my senior year of high school, and it’s held up surprisingly well. Installing it was easy, and the XMP profile made hitting 3600MHz simple. The heat spreaders look clean, and it fits nicely in my build. That said, as I’ve moved into college-level workloads, I’ve noticed it struggles a bit with heavier multitasking and modern games at max settings. It’s great for school projects, light gaming, and general use, but don’t expect it to be top-tier performance. All in all, it’s a solid kit for beginners or high school builds—just know it’s not the “future-proof” option for more demanding setups.
reviews.author: Elijah b.

reviews.title: 100% worth the investment
reviews.comment: Pretty speedy ram, especially when it's set to the highest speed. Looks good in most PCs if you're going with a red and black build. Quality is pretty good and well built, It can also handle really heavy duty gaming especially if you clock it to the highest speed. Stability is good handles my day-to-day task and gaming. :)
reviews.author: Drake

reviews.title: Update: NOW stable at 3600
reviews.comment: I bought the 16gb kit of 3600-18-22-22-42 for a build using a Gigabyte B550m DS3H mb (recent BIOS) and AMD 5700G APU. I really want at least 3600 speed to help with the integrated graphics in the 5700G; however, I cannot get it to boot when set to the advertised 3600 XMP profile. The memory works fine at the slow JEDEC 2400 profile speed, and I can get it to work fine at 3200 speed with the XMP  sub timings, but not 3600. I tried loosening the sub timings, and bumping the XMP 1.35 voltage a little up to 1.37, but to no avail - whenever I set the speed to 3600, it won't boot and goes back to the bios and sets the speed at JEDEC 2400. I was hoping this would be a smooth install at a good price, but alas -no. Sure it could be a problem with the motherboard, but I tried some known good 3600 Crucial ram from another machine, this worked fine. Unfortunately, it looks like Crucial has moved on to DDR5 and I can no longer find this ram! So It looks like I will be returning these sticks and try something else. Unfortunately, I'll probably have to pay a little more, but I really want stable 3600.  Two stars because it will boot and work, but not at the advertised speed in my motherboard that has been out for a while and has been well reviewed. Update: After updating the BIOS to F16a (I was running F15, I don't normally like running an *a* version BIOS,  the machine did boot at 3600 and seems to be running stably. Only 4 stars now, instead of the earlier 2, as the F15 BIOS was recent enough that the ram should have worked with it. I almost returned it, but will keep it now.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer
